source: 上外版选择性必修三 Unit 3 同主题完形(百慕大三角/嫦娥四号/亚特兰蒂斯/穿越撒哈拉/天生的探索者/深海探测技术)。选项同词性,答案唯一,与阅读/听力关不撞篇。

passages.title: The Bermuda Triangle
passages.text: The Bermuda Triangle is an area of the Atlantic Ocean that has long been a (1)____ to people around the world. Since 1945, more than a hundred ships and planes are said to have (2)____ there, often without leaving a single (3)____ behind. Many strange (4)____ have been put forward to explain these losses, but few people are truly (5)____ by them. Some writers blamed sudden storms; others (6)____ to magnetic forces or even aliens. Careful scientists, however, (7)____ that the area is no more dangerous than many other busy parts of the sea. They point out that heavy traffic and bad weather can easily (8)____ accidents. In (9)____, records show that ships go missing here no more often than (10)____. Even so, the puzzle of the Triangle still excites the imagination of millions.

questions.explanation: a mystery to people 对人们而言是个谜。
have disappeared there 在那里消失,与'没留下痕迹'呼应。
without leaving a single clue 没留下一丝线索。
strange theories 奇怪的理论(被提出来解释)。
convinced by them 被它们说服。
pointed to magnetic forces 把原因指向磁力。
scientists insist that 科学家坚持认为。
cause accidents 引发事故。
in fact 事实上。
no more often than elsewhere 不比别处更频繁。

passages.title: China's Journey to the Far Side of the Moon
passages.text: In early 2019, China made history when its Chang'e-4 probe became the first to land softly on the far (1)____ of the moon. This part of the moon can never be seen from Earth, so the (2)____ was extremely difficult. After a long journey, the probe (5)____ touched down and began to explore. It took clear (6)____ of the strange grey surface and studied the soil with care. Scientists hope these samples will help them (7)____ how the moon was formed long ago. The (8)____ was praised around the world as a great step forward. It also showed that the desire to (9)____ the unknown is as strong as ever. One day, such work may even help humans build a research (10)____ on the moon.

questions.explanation: the far side of the moon 月球的远端。
the landing was difficult 着陆很困难。
travel directly 直接传送(信号)。
carry messages between 在两者间传递信息。
finally touched down 终于着陆,后文确实落了地。
took clear pictures 拍下清晰的照片。
help them understand 帮助他们理解。
the mission was praised 这次任务受到称赞。
explore the unknown 探索未知。
a research station 一座科研站。

passages.title: The Lost City of Atlantis
passages.text: Thousands of years ago, the Greek writer Plato told of a great island (1)____ called Atlantis. According to his story, it was a rich and powerful (2)____ that suddenly sank beneath the waves in a single day and night. Ever since, people have (3)____ whether such a place ever truly existed. Some treasure hunters have spent their whole lives (4)____ for its ruins under the sea, but no one has found solid (5)____. A few researchers (6)____ that the tale was based on a real island near Greece, which was partly destroyed by a volcano long ago. Others (7)____ that Plato simply made the whole thing up to teach a lesson. The (8)____ that a wonderful city lies hidden somewhere on the ocean floor is hard to give up. Perhaps the (9)____ of Atlantis will never be solved. Still, the search goes on, (10)____ all the doubts of careful scientists.

questions.explanation: an island kingdom 一个岛国。
a rich and powerful nation 富强的国度。
wondered whether 想知道是否……。
searching for its ruins 寻找它的遗迹。
solid evidence 确凿证据。
researchers believe that 研究者认为。
others argue that 另一些人则主张。
the idea that 一座城藏在海底这一想法。
the mystery of Atlantis 亚特兰蒂斯之谜。
despite all the doubts 尽管有种种怀疑。

passages.title: Crossing the Great Sahara
passages.text: The Sahara is the largest hot (1)____ in the world, stretching across the north of Africa. For thousands of years, brave traders (2)____ its endless sand to carry salt and gold from one side to the other. Travelling there was always (3)____, for the days were burning hot and the nights were bitterly cold. Without enough water, a person could not (4)____ for long. Guides had to (5)____ the safest path by reading the stars and the shape of the dunes. Even today, with modern cars, crossing the desert is far from (6)____. Sandstorms can (7)____ a serious danger, hiding the road and turning day into night. Yet the Sahara still (8)____ many explorers, who long to test themselves against its harsh beauty. Each year a few (9)____ travellers set out to cross it on foot or by camel. For them, the empty desert is not a place to fear but a (10)____ to be met.

questions.explanation: the largest hot desert 最大的热带沙漠。
crossed its endless sand 穿越无尽的沙海。
was always difficult,与后文酷热严寒相符。
could not survive for long 无法长久存活。
choose the safest path 选出最安全的路。
far from easy 远非易事。
pose a serious danger 构成严重危险。
still attracts many explorers 仍吸引许多探险者。
a few brave travellers 几位勇敢的旅人。
a challenge to be met 一项有待迎接的挑战。

passages.title: Born to Explore
passages.text: Human beings seem to be born (1)____. From the earliest times, our ancestors were never (2)____ to stay in one place. They climbed the highest mountains, crossed wide oceans, and walked into empty deserts simply to see what lay (3)____. This deep (4)____ to discover new things has shaped the whole history of our species. Every time one question is answered, a new one (5)____. When we finally reached the moon, we at once began to dream of the (6)____ beyond it. Some people ask why we should (7)____ so much time and money on exploration. The answer is that curiosity makes us (8)____ as human beings. Exploring teaches us about the world and, just as importantly, about (9)____. As long as there are unknown places to reach, there will always be people (10)____ enough to go and find them.

questions.explanation: born explorers 天生的探索者。
never content to stay 从不满足于待着不动。
see what lay beyond 看看更远处有什么。
this deep desire 这种强烈的渴望。
a new one appears 又冒出一个新问题。
dream of the stars beyond it 梦想月球之外的群星。
spend so much time and money 花费大量时间金钱。
makes us grow 让我们成长。
about ourselves 也认识我们自己(we → ourselves)。
curious enough to go 好奇到愿意前往。

passages.title: New Tools for the Deep Sea
passages.text: Exploring the deep ocean is one of the hardest (1)____ that scientists face today. These vehicles carry bright lights and cameras, so that researchers can (4)____ creatures that have never been seen before. Some are sent down without any people inside and are (5)____ from a ship on the surface. Thanks to this modern (6)____, we now know that life exists even at the very (7)____ of the sea. There is no (10)____ that the deep sea will keep surprising explorers for many years to come.

questions.explanation: one of the hardest tasks 最艰难的任务之一。

resist the huge pressure 顶住巨大的压力。
study creatures 研究海洋生物。
controlled from a ship 由船上操控。
this modern technology 这种现代技术。
at the very bottom of the sea 在海的最底层。
brings back new facts 带回新的事实。
a complete mystery 一个完全的谜。
there is no doubt that 毫无疑问。
